assessment_summary:
Step 1: Let G be an arbitrary 3-connected cubic bipartite graph. (Justified)
Step 2: Since G is a regular bipartite graph, it has a perfect matching M by Hall's Marriage Theorem. (Justified)
Step 3: Removing the edges of M from G leaves a 2-regular graph, which must be a collection of disjoint cycles that span all vertices of G. (Justified)
Step 4: Because G is 3-connected, it must be possible to find a perfect matching such that the remaining graph is a single spanning cycle, thus making G Hamiltonian. (Unjustified. This is equivalent to Tutte's 1971 conjecture, which was disproved by J.D. Horton in 1982. The Horton graph and Georges graph are known counterexamples of 3-connected cubic bipartite graphs that are non-Hamiltonian.)
